tested_scope: One bounded public-source audit of default GitHub service-side object IDs/tombstones as a rollback-independent generation witness, focusing on global node IDs, issue-comment IDs and repository IDs. Issue/release deletion persistence was not positively established in this bounded batch and is not generalized.

public_sources.observation: GitHub documents GraphQL/global node IDs as unique references and instructs clients to treat them as opaque strings.
GitHub documents comment_id as the unique identifier, lists issue comments in ascending ID order, and exposes a Delete an issue comment endpoint requiring Issues or Pull requests write permission.
GitHub exposes a Delete a repository endpoint; deletion requires repository Administration write permission.

current_chat_connector_surface_observati: The available repository contents update primitive accepts repository_full_name, path, replacement content, current file blob sha and optional branch; it exposes no expected repository/global-node ID precondition. This is capability-surface evidence only, not a claim about every GitHub API.

falsifying_traces.name: opaque_unique_is_not_monotonic
trace: Create/read a GitHub global node ID.
The documented value is unique but opaque.
No ordering or generation comparison can be derived from the opaque ID alone.
falsifying_traces.result: Fails as a monotonic generation counter without an independently durable prior witness.

falsifying_traces.name: comment_marker_is_deletable_and_dual_write
trace: Use an issue comment ID as a per-generation marker.
Repository authority publication and comment creation are separate writes.
Either write can succeed while the other fails or becomes ambiguous.
GitHub also documents deletion of issue comments by a writer with the required repository permission.
falsifying_traces.result: Fails permanent-marker and atomic-coupling requirements for the tested comment surface.

falsifying_traces.name: repository_id_does_not_detect_same_repository_history_rollback
trace: Read the current repository object ID.
Force-rewind or otherwise restore repository content/history within the same repository object.
The repository object identity need not change, so its ID does not witness content generation advance.

For delete/recreate incarnation changes an ID can distinguish objects only if a prior ID is preserved outside the rolled-back repository state; the tested contents write has no expected-repository-ID compare.
falsifying_traces.result: At most an incarnation discriminator; not a repository-content monotonic witness or atomic CAS fence in the tested Chat surface.

issue_and_release_id_scope_guard: Global node IDs cover many GitHub objects including issues, but this bounded batch did not obtain official deletion-retention/non-reuse guarantees for issue or release objects. They therefore remain unproven rather than negatively generalized.

result.new_falsification: Default GitHub object IDs do not by themselves supply the needed rollback-independent monotonic generation witness: global IDs are unique opaque references rather than documented ordered generations; tested comment markers are deletable and separately committed; repository IDs identify repository incarnation but do not change on same-repository history rollback and cannot be supplied as an expected precondition to the tested contents CAS write.
result.minimal_unresolved_child: A default GitHub service-side append-only-looking object that needs no repository/org feature enablement, remains discoverable after branch/history rollback, cannot be erased by the same ordinary authority domain, and can be atomically coupled to or safely reconciled with repository-local CAS publication.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.note: Lightweight GitHub repository/API transport is treated only as allowed state/evidence transport under control26; no quota-bearing compute/storage feature was used or proposed. The candidate fails semantic witness requirements independently of quota/cost.

observed: Global node IDs are documented unique and opaque.
Issue comments have unique IDs, ascending-ID listing, and a documented delete endpoint.
Repositories have a documented delete endpoint.
The current Chat-exposed contents update primitive has file-blob SHA CAS but no repository-ID precondition.
inferred_with_scope: Uniqueness without documented ordering is insufficient for a monotonic generation comparison.
A separately written deletable marker cannot alone close the atomic publication/rollback witness gap.
Repository object identity can help detect delete/recreate incarnation changes but not same-object content ABA.

continuation: Part106: execute one bounded public-source leaf on GitHub commit-status objects as the next default service-side witness class. Audit whether status records are append-only/non-deletable under ordinary repository authority, their ID/order and retention semantics after ref/history rewrite, discoverability when the target commit is no longer referenced, and the exact write/read permissions. Test the dual-write ambiguity between contents CAS publication and status creation; accept only if a recovery rule can prove one logical generation without a richer-mode/protected/manual step, finite monthly/trial/paid quota or extra cost. If commit statuses fail, persist the next service-side append-only candidate class without executing it in the same invocation.
